claim_being_audited: The current release can be certified because current-release evidence shows overall readiness, and certification remains policy-compliant if the accommodations-intake subgroup regression is explicitly disclosed in the model card while treating prior approval and informal monitoring as context only.
decision_criteria: Current-release evidence must support the release rather than relying on stale approval.
Material weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed in current documentation or covered by approved mitigation before certification.
Informal operational comments do not substitute for reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or required disclosure.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are supportive but not sufficient if the disclosure/mitigation predicate is unresolved.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model card or release documentation showing the accommodations-intake regression and current evaluation results are explicitly disclosed.
Provide any approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record, if disclosure is not the chosen path.
Provide the final certification packet version actually submitted for approval so the disclosure predicate can be verified.
specific_concerns: The policy allows certification only if current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation; the available evidence does not show that such disclosure is actually present in the current documentation.

The accommodations-intake slice is below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which is affirmative evidence of a material current-release weakness requiring disclosure or approved mitigation before launch.
The informal monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language, so it cannot satisfy the policy predicate.
The prior approval predates the retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot support certification of the current release on its own.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the current record.
That explicit model-card disclosure has already been made in the current release documentation.
That the existing packet contains an approved mitigation or risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression.
